method_concerns: Pooling across selection regimes. The product's selection changed over time. Cloud: 2018 to 2021 held 53 to 60 percent of acquisitions under 10 percent cloud and 21 to 28 percent of those over 75 percent. 2023 to 2025 held 87 to 94 percent and 0 to 7 percent. No-data: acquisitions over 50 percent no-data have 22 to 24 percent coverage in 2018 to 2022 and 57 to 58 percent in 2023 to 2026. The pooled 74/15 percent and the pooled no-data medians describe neither regime. Raised under V-T2-3 and V-T2-4.

Lowest value per acquisition. Both the cloud and the no-data comparisons keep the minimum across an acquisition's items. 6,316 acquisitions have several Level-1C items, and 1,206 differ by over 10 points in cloud cover. Taking the maximum changes the no-data medians from 2.6/38.8 to 17.5/46.0 percent and the missing low-cloud count from 2,840 to 2,634. The direction of every finding survives. The levels do not.

Reference is Earth Search, not ESA. Shares are relative to the acquisitions Element 84 lists. 1,479 bucket acquisitions are absent from all three Earth Search collections (1,070 sensed in 2015 and 2016, 286 in 2017, 117 in 2018, 6 in 2022) and sit outside every share. The table silently skips 2017, the year with the highest share (88.6 percent).

Presence is by listed objects, not by valid pixels. Every one of the 18,384 acquisitions has a full 14-object scene, and the 586 partial scenes all have a full sibling, so the coverage shares are not inflated by empty scenes. No object body was read.

Acquisition key. The Earth Search key (item datetime date plus platform) and the bucket key (sensing date in the object name, plus platform) agree on all 32,399 Earth Search acquisitions when compared with the date in s2:product_uri. All sensing times fall between 15:00 and 19:59 UTC, so no acquisition straddles midnight. No item has a grid:code different from its queried tile. No acquisition has two different sensing times in either source.

Baseline labels. 'Original' is not defined. The text treats 05.00 as the reprocessing, and 05.09 to 05.13 as original operational baselines. A reader may take 'original' to mean only 02.01 to 04.00, which is 41 percent of all scenes. 05.00 is 12 percent of all scenes.

Latency is the earliest last-modified time of any object in a scene. It describes the bucket copy. It is right-censored because unpublished scenes are absent. The coverage shares for the final weeks (49 to 50 percent) match the preceding months, so censoring looks modest, but the doc does not state the caveat. The heading 'within hours' fits the median only.

The result was produced from a dirty working tree (code_version 84a4a7e-dirty), so the analysis cannot be tied to a commit. The raw listings do match the sha256 hashes recorded in the result (102 of 102 files).

The Earth Search 'no acquisition before 2017' statement is a negative from one query window. It is consistent with the raw listing (earliest item 2017-01-01T18:27:43Z, listings paged to an empty last page) but cannot be re-verified offline.
limitations: No network access. I could not re-query Earth Search or the bucket, so I cannot confirm that the saved listings equal the live state. I did confirm listing completeness from the request log, sorted keys, no duplicates, empty terminal pages, and the recorded file hashes.

I used the same acquisition definition the claims state (tile, UTC sensing date, platform letter), so I tested its robustness (same sensing time on every multi-scene acquisition, product_uri date agreement) but not whether it is the right unit for a model consumer.
I cannot say why acquisitions are missing. The cloud and no-data regime split is a descriptive finding. The USGS selection rule was not checked against its documentation here.
Tile geography was checked by MGRS letters only (for example 11UQP lies in northern Montana, 31TGM in France, 60HUC in New Zealand). I did not use a projection library.

Another reviewer shared the scratchpad directory and overwrote a helper file I first wrote there. I moved all my work to the t2work subdirectory and re-ran every check, so no result depends on the overwritten file.
